output.title: The real limit of dual running
output.body:
Dual running is just a workflow decision: keep the manual process alive while a new AI-assisted path runs beside it. For an owner-operator, that only makes sense when you are already weighing repeat work against hiring or automation.

The catch is overlap. While both paths exist, someone still has to review outputs, spot mismatches, and decide which path is the source of truth. For money movement and other high-risk decisions, human approval stays mandatory. No spreadsheet gets a vote.

Bareni’s normal sequence is simple: identify one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and if it does, define pilot scope, measures, and the working MVP. That is method, not a promise of results.

The practical question is this: how much owner time goes into the workflow each week, and how many decision points genuinely need your judgment? If the answer is “a lot,” dual running will be expensive for long. If it is narrow, a short pilot may be enough to see whether the new path deserves to stay.
